corrections.claimed_speedup: Startup geomean on AMD EPYC 7763 relative to the per-case fastest runtime (lower is better): DLR-wasm-interpreter x10.95 versus Wasmtime (Cranelift) x1634.19, Wasmer (Cranelift) x1484.15, Wasmtime (Winch) x298.15, Wasmer (Singlepass) x162.12 and V8 x33.27; about 149x faster startup than Wasmtime (Cranelift) and 136x faster than Wasmer (Cranelift) (derived from page data). corrections.compiler_and_flags: wasmi-benchmarks (github.com/wasmi-labs/wasmi-benchmarks) Cargo.toml [profile.bench] lto = "fat", codegen-units = 1, run as 'cargo criterion --bench criterion --all-features ... startup/' (criterion 0.8.2; sample_size 10, 2 s measurement, 1 s warm-up). Rust toolchain: .github/workflows/startup.yml uses dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable with no rust-toolchain file, so the rustc version is not recorded; the C/C++ runtimes are built with gcc-15/g++-15 (.github/actions/install-dependencies). corrections.hardware: AMD EPYC 7763 (plot title and data/amd-epyc-7763 directory). This is the CPU of GitHub's ubuntu-latest runners and the suite's startup.yml workflow runs there, so the data probably come from a shared CI VM (not confirmed). The plots repo also holds Apple M2 Pro, Apple M4 Pro, Intel i7700 and Intel Xeon Platinum 8573C data, not read here.
corrections.caveats: The suite is maintained and run by the Wasmi author, so it is third-party for every runtime except Wasmi. Ratios were read from the SVG text labels and checked against the raw criterion data, which reproduce the startup geomeans exactly. The measured crate is dlr-wasm-interpreter 0.2.0 (current crates.io release). Startup is decode + validate + instantiate of 7 modules (erc20 to ffmpeg); the win is an in-place interpreter versus optimizing JITs, which is expected. Against other interpreters it is not the fastest: Wasmi v2 lazy-translation (also validates eagerly) is x10.66, Wasmi v2 lazy x1.37 and Wasm3 lazy x2.77, and V8 starts faster on the two largest modules (ffmpeg 35.5 ms vs 127.1 ms, spidermonkey 10.9 ms vs 32.9 ms). Startup-only win: execution geomean on the same CPU (plot geomean-execute.svg) is x122.00, about 7 times slower than WAMR fast-interpreter x17.07 (derived from page data), over 20 of 21 cases (no tail calls); the committed criterion.json gives a different execute geomean (98.25), so the execute plot came from another run. Data probably from a shared GitHub Actions VM. The project's own README gives no performance numbers.

notes: Every number in the record is on the plot and in the raw data. Downgraded A to B only for the unrecorded rustc version and suite commit.
